title: The Unwritten Harbor
premise: In 1913, Juniper Sterling drives for a suffragist organizer and secretly reads the letters she carries, learning the movement's secrets before the state does. When a census taker begins asking pointed questions about the harbor workshop that prints banned pamphlets, Juniper discovers the raid is coming and must choose between protecting the woman they serve and exposing a betrayal within the movement itself. Loyalties fracture as Juniper smuggles the printing press's evidence to safety, confronts the informer, and finally testifies to what they know — outside any court. The workshop burns, but the work survives: Juniper inherits the route, the letters, and the burden of reading them.
about_author: Vesper Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffrage-era correspondence in coastal New England. They write historical fiction about the people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Weight of Letters
chapters.summary: Juniper Sterling, POV. Establishes Juniper's routine: driving for organizer Marguerite Vale, reading letters by lamplight before delivery. We learn the harbor workshop prints the pamphlets. Emotional beat: quiet longing for belonging in a movement that uses but doesn't see them.

chapters.title: A Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A census taker lingers at the workshop, asking about ownership, printing equipment, and who sleeps there. Marguerite deflects smoothly, but Juniper notices the man wrote nothing down — he already had his answers. Emotional beat: first cold drop of dread.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dusk
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Marguerite gives Juniper sealed orders: move the press's type cases before week's end. Juniper measures what can be carried in the motorcar and what must be abandoned. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of being trusted at last.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Workshop printer Elias Boone's POV. Elias hides the type while watching the census taker sketch the building from a rowboat. He suspects someone inside is talking. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root in an old man's pride.

chapters.title: What Juniper Read
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A letter reveals a raid is scheduled and — more damning — that someone inside supplied the address. Juniper must decide whether to tell Marguerite without revealing they read the letter. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Long Game
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She knows more than she says; the raid may be a trap she's willing to spring to expose the government's overreach. She tests Juniper's loyalty with a false errand. Emotional beat: the chill of being a piece on someone's board.

chapters.title: The Informer's Face
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper narrows the suspects to three: Elias, treasurer Adela Finch, and young volunteer Tom Wrenn. A staged letter, left deliberately readable, flushes out a reaction. Emotional beat: the sickness of suspecting friends.

chapters.title: Adela's Debts
chapters.summary: Adela Finch's POV. Adela is drowning in her late husband's debts and a federal man has offered to make them vanish. She hasn't given anything yet — but she hasn't refused. Emotional beat: desperation dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Carrying the Type
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The first smuggling run: type cases hidden under fish crates, a checkpoint at the harbor road, Juniper lying smoothly for the first time in their life. Emotional beat: transformation — the reader of letters becomes a writer of lies.

chapters.title: Tom Wrenn Confesses
chapters.summary: Tom Wrenn's POV. Tom, terrified, admits he answered census questions innocently, not knowing the workshop mattered. Juniper realizes the informer is someone else — but Tom's slip has already armed the raid. Emotional beat: pity for a boy who broke nothing and everything.

chapters.title: Marguerite Refuses to Run
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper begs Marguerite to abandon the workshop; she refuses — the next pamphlet run is timed to an important vote and cannot wait. Emotional beat: fury at a leader who spends other people's safety for principle.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A second intercepted letter names the date: Thursday. It also names the informer's codeword, which Juniper recognizes as Adela's husband's old regimental phrase. Emotional beat: certainty arriving like a verdict.

chapters.title: Adela's Choice
chapters.summary: Adela's POV. The federal man presses Adela for the press's new location. She stalls, torn between debt and the women who fed her when she had nothing. Emotional beat: the exact width of the line between survival and betrayal.

chapters.title: Wednesday Night
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Final preparations: Elias's last printing run, the press itself too heavy to move, Juniper dismantling it alone through the night. Marguerite watches from the doorway and, for once, helps. Emotional beat: grudging, wordless reconciliation.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Thursday dawn: officers arrive to find the workshop stripped, Elias waiting with tea and a lawyer's card. They arrest him anyway. The building is sealed, not burned — yet. Emotional beat: defiance curdling into helplessness.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper delivers the rescued type to a farmhouse outside town, where the movement will print in exile. Adela is there — and so is the federal man's motorcar passing on the road. Emotional beat: the safe house may not be safe.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Mill Road
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper corners Adela alone and lays out the evidence: the codeword, the debts, the timing. Adela neither denies nor confesses; she asks what Juniper would have done. Emotional beat: the uncomfortable recognition of a shared desperation.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite refuses to hand Adela to the authorities — the movement doesn't feed its people to the courts. Instead she imposes her own sentence: exile from the movement and public silence. Emotional beat: justice as mercy with teeth.

chapters.title: The Fire
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The sealed workshop burns in the night — arson, though no one claims it. Juniper suspects Adela destroying evidence of her own dealings, or the government erasing its own informer's trail. Emotional beat: grief for a place that was never theirs, and rage without a target.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At Elias's hearing, Juniper testifies to what the letters contained — implicating the census operation itself. It's not a courtroom victory; it's a record, entered into the world. Emotional beat: truth spoken plainly, at personal cost.

chapters.title: The Route Passes On
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Marguerite, worn down and half-blind, formally gives Juniper the letter route — the reading, the carrying, the choosing. Juniper accepts, knowing now what it costs. Emotional beat: belonging finally earned, and feared.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Harbor
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Months later, Juniper drives the coastal road with pamphlets under fish crates, past the workshop's blackened shell. A new letter waits to be read. Juniper opens it. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won resolve — the harbor is gone, but the writing continues.
